E01.subtitle: The Celestial Loom
E01.plaque: A universe whose physics are programmable. Pull one thread and the consequences propagate.
E01.problem: What does a world look like if its fundamental material behaves like software?
E01.made: A continuity-heavy science-fantasy universe with programmable Starsilk at its centre, held together by written rules about what canon forbids as much as what it permits.
E01.interaction: Pull the fundamental threads of the loom. Each change propagates visibly through the cosmological model above you.
E01.explore: Walk beneath the loom. The relationships between star nodes read differently from underneath than from the gallery floor.

E02.subtitle: Thirty-seven Entries
E02.plaque: One Egg, thirty-five strains, one Mother. A terraforming taxonomy presented as a service manual.
E02.problem: How do you document a species that exists to perform an industrial process?
E02.made: A thirty-seven entry field compendium organised by five archetypes, with fixed formatting doctrine and a canon-correction record.
E02.interaction: Select a source-grounded process reference. The central Egg opens an abstract process glyph; it does not claim an undocumented specimen morphology.
E02.explore: Four canonical process references and one clearly marked taxonomy abstraction stand around the Egg. Mother is visible as a distant abstract relief.

E03.subtitle: Six Months Over Virgil
E03.plaque: Not an explosion — a dismantling, carried out with intent across six months.
E03.problem: How do you tell one event as a song, a story, a visual production and an interactive tour without any of them becoming an adaptation?
E03.made: A Starsilk production in four simultaneous media, all developed against a single six-month dismantling timeline.
E03.interaction: Turn the dismantling dial. The station segment reconfigures from Month Zero through Month Six.
E03.explore: Enter the station fragment. The interior changes with the dial.

E04.subtitle: Mapping Negative Space
E04.plaque: A canon is not only what it has said. It is also what it has forbidden, contradicted, and left open.
E04.problem: How do you know what a fictional universe still permits you to invent?
E04.made: A deterministic local engine that assigns evidence states to canon claims and maps the possibility space that remains legal.
E04.interaction: Select a canon fact. Legal possibilities illuminate, contradictions close, and unresolved regions stay dark — because absence of a rule is not permission.
E04.explore: The possibility graph is volumetric. Walk into it and inspect relationships from inside the structure.

E05.subtitle: Weaving the Material
E05.plaque: The moment the setting's central material stopped being a description and became something you could hold.
E05.problem: Does the invented material actually have coherent rules, or only convincing ones?
E05.made: A generative instrument that turns drawn paths into woven Starsilk compositions obeying the canon rules for tension and interference.
E05.interaction: Draw a path through the air above the loom. The mechanism weaves it into a thread composition.
E05.explore: Completed fibres extend outward from the loom as a small sculpture that persists while you are in the room.

E06.subtitle: Four Layers Down
E06.plaque: Drakken organs are stages of a process. The anatomy is a pipeline diagram.
E06.problem: How do you teach the structure of a creature without teaching things canon never established?
E06.made: A forensic anatomy reference with four view layers and a hard separation between canon specimens and deliberately non-canon teaching surrogates.
E06.interaction: Cycle each table through external, skeletal, energy-process and section views.
E06.explore: Three tables stand side by side. The surrogate specimen is marked and separated — the marking is part of the exhibit.

E07.subtitle: The Process Lock
E07.plaque: Gorevault gathers and refines. Ringthroat makes sky. Collapse the two and the world stops changing.
E07.problem: Is the terraforming process described in the Compendium actually coherent, or only plausible?
E07.made: A deterministic simulation of the full Drakken pipeline: collection, gathering, rendering and refinement into feedstock, then feedstock into SKY.
E07.interaction: Deploy strains against the world above the engineering floor. The pipeline executes in order and the planet visibly changes.
E07.explore: Walk the full circle of the engineering floor. The world transforms differently depending on which side you watch from.

E08.subtitle: The Siege Wall Is an Absence
E08.plaque: From an inhabited world the Siege Wall is not a structure. It is the shape of what has been removed.
E08.problem: How do you render the extinguishing of a sky without turning an absence into an object?
E08.made: An observatory that plays back stellar extinction in canon order, under a hard visual rule forbidding any masonry, lattice or grid reading.
E08.interaction: Begin the reconstruction. Stars leave the sky in the order canon requires.
E08.explore: Three telescope stations give genuinely different views of the same event. The difference is the point.

E09.subtitle: The Building Before This One
E09.plaque: Earlier attempts at this museum, preserved rather than hidden — including the one that proved a single file could not hold it.
E09.problem: Is this museum a restoration of the previous artifact, or a new lineage?
E09.made: A record of the Museum of Me and Reliquary concepts, the large single-file Three.js artifact they produced, and the decision to build this version as a separate product.
E09.interaction: Turn the timeline control. Earlier museum concepts rise from the maquette table as layered models.
E09.explore: The final layer is the building you are standing in.

E10.subtitle: Three Generations, Each Smaller
E10.plaque: A platform became a command-line tool became a folder of Markdown. The folder is the one still running.
E10.problem: What is the smallest system that can hold a body of canon for years?
E10.made: Three successive canon-management systems: a platform architecture study, a local-first tool with schemas and transfer packets, and finally a versioned vault of plain files.
E10.interaction: Feed the same lore record into each machine in turn and watch how its representation — and the machinery required — changes.
E10.explore: The three machines are connected in sequence. Each is visibly simpler than the one before it.

E11.subtitle: Context That Survives the Conversation
E11.plaque: Project context that lives only in a conversation is project context you are going to lose.
E11.problem: How does a project remember itself across tools, sessions and years?
E11.made: A handoff builder with an approval gate, an append-only project record in version control, and a long-horizon progress tracker.
E11.interaction: Assemble a handoff from evidence blocks. Claims without supporting evidence are rejected by the mechanism.
E11.explore: The documentation chain runs the length of the alcove; each stage physically refuses input the previous stage did not justify.

E12.subtitle: Which Kind of Claim Is This?
E12.plaque: The useful question about a statement is rarely whether it is true. It is what kind of move it is making.
E12.problem: Readers fail to notice when a text shifts from reporting evidence to framing it.
E12.made: An offline single-file analysis tool that classifies spans of writing as evidence, interpretation, framing, inference or unsupported claim.
E12.interaction: Sort sample statements into the five categories on the evidence table. The table shows the classification the tool would assign, and why.
E12.explore: All examples here are invented. No real dispute, publication or person is analysed in this room.

E13.subtitle: What Actually Reproduced
E13.plaque: A prompt manual worth keeping records the techniques that failed alongside the ones that worked.
E13.problem: Which instructions to a generative music model actually change the output, and which are ignored?
E13.made: A durable songwriting codex covering lyric structure, narration, style-prompt grammar and parameter behaviour, assembled from repeated testing.
E13.interaction: Switch between original project excerpts at the desk and raise or lower the simplified arrangement layers.
E13.explore: Instrument and waveform objects in the room respond spatially to whatever is currently playing.

E14.subtitle: Prompts as Components
E14.plaque: The reusable part of a prompt is usually the constraint list, not the description.
E14.problem: Generative prompts are rewritten from scratch every time, and their hard-won negative constraints are lost first.
E14.made: A registry of visual-prompt templates with batch syntax and stored negative constraints, and a beginner-safe environment for learning to build software conversationally.
E14.interaction: Combine deterministic prompt blocks in the assembly machine. The rendered scene beyond the glass changes to match — no external service involved.
E14.explore: Constraint blocks are physically different from description blocks, and the machine will not run without them.

E15.subtitle: Routing the Work
E15.plaque: An orchestration system should not own the memory it orchestrates, or it becomes impossible to replace.
E15.problem: How do several different AI development tools share one project's context and hand work to each other?
E15.made: Two orchestration harnesses: one assembling workflows, context and specialist agents around durable external persistence, one attempting interoperability between separate coding agents.
E15.interaction: Route a task through the rack: request, context assembly, specialist selection, validation, handoff.
E15.explore: Persistence sits outside the rack, physically separate, connected by a single cable.

E16.subtitle: Four Generations of the Same Idea
E16.plaque: One feature shipped to three platforms triples the maintenance before it doubles the audience.
E16.problem: A media workflow was rebuilt repeatedly as the delivery strategy changed underneath it.
E16.made: A cross-platform casting application, its native Android successor, a recovered creative application, and a native media utility with bundled tooling.
E16.interaction: Run a media workflow across the bench: input, trim, convert, transcribe, output. Each device generation handles the same job differently.
E16.explore: The devices are arranged chronologically. Each is smaller in scope than the one before it.

E17.subtitle: Speech That Never Leaves the Machine
E17.plaque: Five voice projects, one requirement: recognition and synthesis run locally, and audio is not transmitted.
E17.problem: Dictation and voice synthesis are useful everywhere and trustworthy almost nowhere.
E17.made: System-wide macOS dictation with local recognition, a separate Android input method, a multi-provider synthesis application, a voice-cloning fork, and a thin client for models running on a larger machine.
E17.interaction: Select a prerecorded sample and compare raw transcription, refined transcription, synthesised voice and command interpretation at the four stations.
E17.explore: No microphone permission is requested. Every sample in this room is prerecorded.

E18.subtitle: Software Shaped by a Dog
E18.plaque: These are systems named after Dexter. Dexter himself is elsewhere in this building, and the distinction is deliberate.
E18.problem: An assistant that forgets its own rules between sessions cannot be relied on for anything exacting.
E18.made: A persona and continuity system governing voice and exactness, a local assistant with inspectable append-only memory, and a self-hosted community moderation bot.
E18.interaction: Route a request among the agent roles and watch which memory each one is permitted to read and write.
E18.explore: The memory column is append-only: entries can be pinned or marked forgotten, but the mark itself remains visible.

E19.subtitle: Motion as Command
E19.plaque: A novel input method needs a boring fallback, or it becomes a novelty that gets uninstalled.
E19.problem: Can physical gestures with a phone safely drive a desktop machine?
E19.made: A paired phone-and-desktop bridge converting trained motion gestures into commands from an explicit allowlist, with manual equivalents for everything.
E19.interaction: Take hold of the phone model and tilt it. The desktop station responds to the gesture events in real time.
E19.explore: Your gesture trajectories remain in the air as visible spatial ribbons until they fade.

E20.subtitle: What the Tool Declines to Do
E20.plaque: In destructive tooling, the features you refuse to build are as much of the design as the ones you ship.
E20.problem: Storage and cleanup utilities have a long history of deleting things people wanted and overstating what they recovered.
E20.made: A reversible approval-gated macOS disk auditor, a non-destructive on-device image sorter, and an Android storage explainer that refuses to overclaim.
E20.interaction: Sort synthetic files across the bench. Destructive operations are physically unavailable — the mechanism has no such lever.
E20.explore: Every file on this bench is synthetic. The exhibit has no access to any real filesystem.

E21.subtitle: The Artifact the Institution Asks For
E21.plaque: Software for a crisis has to produce what the institution requires, not a better internal model of the problem.
E21.problem: Institutional processes fail people who cannot produce an accurate chronology with evidence attached.
E21.made: A local-first emergency casefile application for housing, benefits, utilities and medical administration, and a browser extension improving AI workflow surfaces.
E21.interaction: Using an entirely fictional situation, assemble a chronology, attach evidence to each event, and produce a next-action packet.
E21.explore: The situation on this table is invented. No real case record, correspondence or personal document appears in this museum.

E22.subtitle: Making Things That Make Things
E22.plaque: Three creative tools whose lineages show the same lesson: some requirements cannot be retrofitted.
E22.problem: Creative tools accumulate requirements — collaboration, offline operation, target-specific output — that reshape their architecture rather than extending it.
E22.made: An offline prompt-shaping menu-bar application, a hosted image-generation service with durable persistence, and a collaborative whiteboard rebuilt across three generations.
E22.interaction: Draw directly on the design table. Your marks appear on its surface and connect into the shared composition.
E22.explore: The table surface is a live drawing texture. What visitors draw persists for the length of your visit.

E23.subtitle: Composition and Boundary
E23.plaque: Combining ordinary data layers produces genuinely new questions. The composition is the contribution.
E23.problem: Geospatial and language tools are individually common and rarely combined or made private.
E23.made: A tactical globe layering flights, satellites, seismic events, fires, undersea cables and tectonics into one correlatable view, and an offline in-browser speech translator.
E23.interaction: Choose a location on the globe and raise the layers. At the language wall, run a controlled translation example — entirely offline.
E23.explore: No live map service is contacted. Every layer and translation here is bundled sample data.

E24.subtitle: A Campaign as a Database
E24.plaque: Content-heavy game projects are database problems wearing a narrative costume.
E24.problem: A campaign of this size collapses when the same unit is referenced three different ways in three different files.
E24.made: A complete campaign and sourcebook for a strategy game, authored data-first with a purpose-built workflow keeping identifiers, dialogue and mechanics consistent.
E24.interaction: Select regions and artifacts on the campaign table. Terrain rises and campaign paths respond.
E24.explore: Miniature environments lift out of the map surface as you select their regions.

E25.subtitle: Tools Used Under Pressure
E25.plaque: A tool used at a table is judged on interaction cost, not on feature count.
E25.problem: A game master is tracking initiative, hit points, positions and rules simultaneously while people wait.
E25.made: A local encounter-management application with initiative order, hit-point control, a tactical map, bestiary, rules reference, persistence and history.
E25.interaction: Run a single deterministic encounter round: roll, adjust initiative, move a miniature, resolve one action.
E25.explore: The table is small and complete. It is not a D&D engine and does not pretend to be.

E26.subtitle: Built to a Live Deadline
E26.plaque: Tools built under live production deadlines fragment into variants, because there is never a moment to consolidate them.
E26.problem: Broadcast overlays must sit on top of everything, be readable, and never obstruct the thing they annotate.
E26.made: A long-running family of translucent always-on-top desktop overlays with click-through modes and producer-safe controls, and a 16-bit-styled platformer set in real geography.
E26.interaction: Toggle overlay layers and routes on the operations map. Each layer can be made click-through, exactly as in production.
E26.explore: The fragmented repository lineage is shown honestly: the variants are the artifact.

E27.subtitle: Finished
E27.plaque: Among sixty-four projects, this one is complete and playable. A hard deadline did what deadlines do.
E27.problem: Scope grows until something external stops it.
E27.made: A mobile-first rhythm game made as a birthday gift, in which Dexter catches treats, avoids sharks and fills a party meter toward a celebratory finale.
E27.interaction: Three linked mechanisms in the cabinet, each escalating the result of the last.
E27.explore: Small footprint, strong personality. The cabinet takes up less space than most cases in this wing.

E28.subtitle: The Interface Is the Game
E28.plaque: In management games the interface is not the presentation layer. It is the entire mechanism.
E28.problem: A player must read threat, resources and options at a glance without the screen becoming noise.
E28.made: A station survival, management and defence game with extensive interface engineering, packaging and repeated systematic bug sweeps.
E28.interaction: Place fleet pieces on the tactical star table and resolve one deterministic combat turn.
E28.explore: The table reads from any side; information density was the design problem.

E29.subtitle: The Descent Decision
E29.plaque: A prototype that cannot fail is not a prototype. It is a demo.
E29.problem: Is a civilization-scale generation-ship game actually interesting, or only impressive to describe?
E29.made: A modular arkship simulation scoped entirely around one falsifiable hundred-minute prototype built to answer that question before anything larger was committed.
E29.interaction: Explode the ship into its modules — command, habitation, logistics, energy, propulsion — then choose a destination and watch one module deploy.
E29.explore: The ship hangs at full length above the gallery. Walk its axis to read the module sequence.

E30.subtitle: Zero Feedback Delay
E30.plaque: Any authoring tool for something judged by eye must close the feedback loop to nothing.
E30.problem: Visual effects are tuned by watching them, and every second between change and result degrades the result.
E30.made: A browser workbench for procedural ability effects with live control over emitters, forces, lifetime, turbulence and colour behaviour.
E30.interaction: Adjust any control. The effect in the chamber reshapes immediately — there is no apply step.
E30.explore: The chamber is transparent on all sides. The same effect reads differently from each.

E31.subtitle: Two Verbs
E31.plaque: One deeply implemented verb produces more play than six shallow ones.
E31.problem: Two games, opposite in temperament: one about intervention, one about patience.
E31.made: A gesture-first browser god-game built around a single well-developed miracle, and an orbital farming game where power, water and nutrients are one coupled system.
E31.interaction: One side of the portal offers a branching decision. The other lets you plant something and wait for it.
E31.explore: The installation is one object with two faces. Neither side can see the other.

E32.subtitle: A Real Town, Compressed
E32.plaque: Real geography is a good starting point and a bad final layout. The editing is the design work.
E32.problem: Actual distances are boring at play speed, but a town that loses its shape stops being recognisable.
E32.made: A rolling collection game set in a compressed model of a real Vancouver Island town, laid out against real map data and running fully offline.
E32.interaction: Take control of the ball. Roll, collect, and grow — one short self-contained level.
E32.explore: The diorama is a miniature neighbourhood. Everything in it is collectible at sufficient size.

E33.subtitle: A 4X in a Browser Tab
E33.plaque: Deterministic world generation is a testing feature first and a player feature second.
E33.problem: Strategy games plateau in the mid-game, and their AI opponents become unreadable.
E33.made: A complete browser 4X with deterministic galaxy generation, factions, AI empires, economy, research, diplomacy, combat, crises and saves.
E33.interaction: Claim nodes on the galactic board, choose one technology, and watch the expansion consequences resolve.
E33.explore: The same seed always produces the same galaxy. Reset the board and it returns identical.

E34.subtitle: The Machinery Behind the Work
E34.plaque: Six infrastructure projects that decide which machine does the work — and where nothing is permitted to go.
E34.problem: Local AI work needs real compute, large private storage and a trustworthy path between machines.
E34.made: A governed access route, a private storage architecture with no public path, a tunnelled local inference integration, an agent control surface, a launcher for the resulting tool sprawl, and a persistent daemon with real permadeath.
E34.interaction: Select a workflow. A pulse travels the sculpture through the exact nodes that workflow touches.
E34.explore: Every address, hostname and identifier in this room is a synthetic example. No credential, key or operational configuration appears anywhere in this museum.

E35.subtitle: The Trust Boundary
E35.plaque: Some data categories decide the architecture before any engineering discussion begins.
E35.problem: Face processing and open-source research both generate exactly the material you least want logged elsewhere.
E35.made: A local-only face-processing stack with no outbound network path, and a fully local research platform where the investigation is never disclosed to a service provider.
E35.interaction: Run the face bay on synthetic generated faces; run the research bay on a fictional investigation. The wall between the bays shows what does not cross it.
E35.explore: The trust-boundary wall is a physical object here because it is the architectural decision both projects are built on.
